target_customer: Banks, credit unions and fintech lenders that must detect forged or fabricated financial documents
problem: Manual review of bank statements, pay stubs and tax forms is slow and inconsistent, and fraudsters forge documents. Inscribe automates document fraud detection.
business_model: B2B SaaS and API for document fraud detection, sold to financial institutions
product_category: Document fraud detection, fintech risk software

founders.name: Ronan Burke
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder/CEO on the YC page; TechCrunch (2024-03-08) names him CEO and co-founder. The company about page says the founding team's early experience at an Irish bank showed manual review was slow; individuals not specified.

founders.name: Conor Burke
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder/CTO on the YC page. No background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Detecting tampered and fabricated documents needs computer vision, document parsing and forensic modeling with limited labeled fraud data, hard for a two person team in 2017.

defensibility.rationale: Accumulated fraud examples and bank workflow integration help. The company says it created the category, but other document automation vendors added fraud detection later.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition. Competition grew in later years; an Inscribe marketing comparison lists Ocrolus, whose fraud product is described as secondary.

market_need_then: The about page says the founders saw slow and inconsistent manual document review at an Irish bank. No 2018 dated market statistics were found.

branding.domain_note: Uses inscribe.ai; inscribe.com history not found.

identity.logo: Inscribe wordmark and mark, not described in detail
identity.voice_and_tone: Fraud fighter themed, engineers scientists and fraud fighters

branding.brand_signature: Claims to have created the document fraud detection category

brand_strength.rationale: Strong category claim and named fintech customers on its site, but little sourced press about the brand itself.

pivots.from: Document fraud detection focused product strategy
pivots.to: New product direction responding to AI advances and higher rates
pivots.why: TechCrunch (2024-03-08) says Inscribe set a new product strategy in Q4 2023 and planned a major launch later in 2024

outcome_analysis: Inscribe raised a $10.5 million Series A in April 2021 and a $25 million Series B in January 2023, for $38 million total, then cut just under 40 percent of staff in January 2024 after missing revenue goals for over a year as higher interest rates hit fintech customers. The company reset its product strategy for AI and still markets to Plaid, Ramp and others, so it is a once fast growing fintech vendor that stalled in a downturn.
notes: Series B stated by TechCrunch and several outlets (Jan 25, 2023). Series A amount, April 2021 date and investors come from the fintechfutures press release title and search snippets because the page returned 403, so investor list is from search summary. Total raised is $38M, exceeding $35.5M recorded, so roughly $2.5M of earlier funding is not found. Inscribe's own Series B blog page carries a Sept 2024 date, likely an update artifact. Competitors: Ocrolus and Informed.IQ evidence found was dated 2023 or later or undated, so list is empty. Brand note: a USPTO record shows INSCRIBE first use Feb 8, 2018.
